explain.say: See editors choose? Editors are the people who decide which stories go on the news. They are called gatekeepers, because they open the gate for a few stories and close it on the rest. They pick what is new, close to home, dramatic or about famous people. What story would you pick?

explain.say: See you see it and you think about it? Researchers found that the news may not tell you what to think, but it strongly shapes what you think about. If a topic is on the news every day, it feels important. This is called agenda setting. What topic has been in the news a lot lately?

faq.q: How do journalists decide what is news?
faq.a: Editors and journalists choose stories that are new, important, close to their audience, unusual or dramatic, or about well-known people. They also think about what their audience wants and what will attract attention.

faq.q: What is a gatekeeper in the news?
faq.a: A gatekeeper is an editor or producer who decides which stories get published or broadcast, and which are left out. Today, social media algorithms also act as gatekeepers.

faq.q: Why do headlines matter so much?
faq.a: Many people read only the headline. Its words and the picture with it shape how a story feels, and dramatic headlines can attract more clicks, even when the story is calmer.
Agenda setting is the idea that the media shapes what people think is important by choosing which topics to cover often. McCombs and Shaw studied it in 1972.
asks: Tell me about you think about it
Does the news control what we think?

faq.q: How can I get a fuller picture of the news?
faq.a: Read or watch more than one trusted source, check who wrote it and why, look for facts behind the headline, and ask whose voices or places are missing.
asks: How do I read news carefully?
How can I avoid one-sided news?

facts: Maxwell McCombs and Donald Shaw's 1972 study of the 1968 US election launched agenda-setting research.
Political scientist Bernard Cohen wrote in 1963 that the press may not tell people what to think, but is very successful at telling them what to think about.
